ops.title: great-docs: _discover_package_exports shared-loader scope
ops.body:
`GreatDocs._discover_package_exports` (great_docs/core.py, ~line 6613) now shares one griffe `GriffeLoader` across the `for name in filtered:` validation loop (~line 6756-6790), matching the pattern already used by `_categorize_api_objects` (~line 7509).

**Why it was previously unshared:** each call to `get_object()` without a `loader=` arg builds a brand-new `GriffeLoader` (`introspect.py:74-75`), which re-parses the whole package from scratch and pays griffe's per-load git-metadata subprocess calls. For a package with ~232 exports this cost ~517s of build time (measured on cc_transcript 0.15.0-era great-docs).

**Why sharing within the loop is safe but sharing across calls/phases is not:** the loop's re-export detection checks `qd_obj.canonical_path` to decide if an object is a re-export from outside the package. That check gives false positives once the loader has extra, unrelated modules pre-loaded — e.g. a type alias like `HandlerFunc = Callable[..., None]` resolves its canonical path back to `typing`, and if `typing` was loaded into the *same* loader by an unrelated earlier call, canonical-path checks for names that legitimately belong to the current package can get confused by residue from that other load. Within a single `_discover_package_exports` invocation, every object loaded through the shared loader is a member of the one package being validated, so that scenario doesn't arise. The loader is still rebuilt fresh on every call to `_discover_package_exports` (no module-level or cross-call cache) to keep that invariant.

Verified via an identity check (stock vs. patched `_discover_package_exports` on cc_transcript — same export list, same order, same re-export/failure classification) and a synthetic type-alias edge case before landing. See branch `perf/source-links-loader` in the `great-docs-s5` worktree.
